description: Per-type splitter output cardinality: contract field vs Program.cs pattern

entries.rationale: The Process(string,string) overload produces a single output file — this is a valid single-extraction usage of the API. The contract output_cardinality=multi describes maximum capability (multi-file split via LowCodeSaveOptions), not a requirement on all examples. Single-output extraction is the simplest valid usage.

entries.api_overload: ExtractPages(string inputFile, string outputFile, int startPageIndex, int pageCount)
entries.rationale: ExtractPages extracts a subset of pages into a single output file — this is page extraction, not full document splitting. The contract output_cardinality=multi describes the full-split-each-page capability. ExtractPages with a single output is a valid, canonical demonstration of the API's extraction functionality.

AddOutput with a single FileDataSource produces one output file — this demonstrates single-page extraction. The PDF Splitter supports multiple AddOutput calls for full multi-file splits, but the minimal example (single output) is valid and correct API usage for a first-page extraction scenario.

conclusion: All three splitter Program.cs files use single-output patterns. This is VALID — the API supports both single-output (extraction/first-page) and multi-output (full split) modes. The contract output_cardinality=multi documents maximum capability, not a constraint on example output count. No Program.cs regeneration is required.
